results.content:
Title: Claude Usage Tracker: A floating widget to track Claude usage limits in real time. | Product Hunt
# Claude Usage Tracker. ## A floating widget to track Claude usage limits in real time. A floating desktop widget that shows your Claude.ai usage limits in real time. Launch tags:Productivity•User Experience•Artificial Intelligence. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Claude Usage Tracker. Wispr Flow: Dictation That Works Everywhere. Wispr Flow: Dictation That Works Everywhere — Stop typing. I use Claude heavily for coding and writing, and I kept hitting the usage limit at the worst possible times — right in the middle of a task. The only way to check was to open Claude.ai, navigate to the settings, and manually look at the usage page. I was doing this constantly throughout the day. I wanted something that just sat on my screen and told me at a glance — like a battery indicator, but for Claude. So I built a small floating widget that shows my usage as a progress bar with a countdown timer. It lives in the system tray and never gets in my way. The Chrome extension handles authentication automatically, so there's no manual token copying or login. Everything stays on your machine — no servers, no accounts. If you're a heavy Claude user on Windows, I hope this saves you from the same frustration. Would love to hear feedback!

Title: Code Meter - Claude Usage Monitor macOS | Better monitoring for Claude Code and Minimax rate limits | Product Hunt
Code Meter - Claude Usage Monitor macOS. ## Better monitoring for Claude Code and Minimax rate limits. ### Engineering & Development. ### LLMs. ### Productivity. ### Marketing & Sales. ### Design & Creative. ### Social & Community. ### Finance. ### AI Agents. ### Trending categories. ### Top reviewed. ### Trending products. ### Top forum threads. Hey everyone, I built Code Meter because I kept getting blindsided by Claude Code rate limits in the middle of deep coding sessions. Checking /usage for claude or going on the Minimax api page to check for usage, felt wrong, so I built the thing I wanted: a tiny menu bar app that shows your usage percentage at all times. A few things I’m proud of:. It doesn’t just show your current percentage. It tells you whether you’re on pace to hit the limit, and roughly when. I keep a small widget on my desktop so I can see my usage without even clicking the menu bar icon. When your usage is stable, it polls less often. When things are moving, it speeds up. Keeps the data fresh without hammering the API. If you use Minimax’s Token Plan for coding, Code Meter tracks that too. Just paste your API key. It’s a native macOS app. SwiftUI, Liquid Glass, no Electron. Runs in the menu bar with no dock icon. Feels like it belongs on your Mac because it does. I’d love to hear what you think and what features you’d want next. Happy to answer any questions.

A family of foundational AI models. # ChatGPT / Gemini / Copilot / Claude/ Perplexity ❓ What are you using? I am using mostly ChatGPT. ### Replies. ChatGPT with a little CoPilot and some Stampede Social (oh, did I plug my upcoming launch? @bigmacher What does it do? @sentry\_co Stampede is a social selling and engagement platform for Instagram. Keeping focused on the AI theme of this thread we do AI analysis of post comments and AI competitive analysis (all on the fly) to help you understand your fans/customers and competition better. @bigmacher That's a really good niche to be in! Phind.com and codemate.bot. I use GPT-4 inside CrawlQ AI, followed by Gemini, then Claude (all three are in Crawlq AI). Why I use CrawlQ instead of using GPT-4, Gemini, and Claude directly? 1. My information is not used by the LLMs 2. I can create multiple campaigns / workspaces, specific to topic of interest, target audience. And these information are processed by CrawlQ AI and is used to give context to my prompts. So I only need to write simple prompts, and the AI knows exactly for which audience and topic and business is my prompt. 3. Because of #2, the output I get is on-brand, on-topic, and resonates with my audience. Right now I am mostly using Gemini Advanced to see if I want to begin paying for it instead of ChatGPT Plus. Google offered a 2-month trial to test it out. So far, I am very happy with it. I am building an app where you will be able to access most of these AIs under a single subscription. ChatGPT is good, but when I tried Claude, to be frank, the output quality was awesome. Knock Knock Jokes for Kids. ChatGPT but very interested in Claude - if only they had an iPhone app. I use chatgpt, but thinking of trying copilot as well. I know only ChatGPT , but will check others .
